planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger has passed in warm soil, or get a jump on the season with an indoor start.

directions: Benary's Giant Purple bears rich violet-purple fully double blooms 4-6 inches wide on tall, sturdy stems bred specifically for professional cut-flower production. Plants hold up well to Gulf Coast summer heat and rain far better than older heirloom giant zinnias, and the long, strong stems make it a top choice for market bouquets and cutting gardens. Succession-sow every two to three weeks for a continuous supply of stems, and space plants a foot apart with good airflow to reduce powdery mildew and Alternaria leaf spot. Deadhead or harvest regularly to keep plants branching and blooming through frost.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

directions: Oklahoma Salmon produces bright salmon-pink 1.5-2.5 inch double and semi-double scabiosa-form blooms in great abundance on compact, sturdy plants. The smaller flower size and high stem count per plant make it especially efficient for cutting gardens and bouquet work, and the series shows less susceptibility to powdery mildew than many large-flowered zinnia types. Thin seedlings for good air circulation and deadhead or harvest continually to keep production high from early summer through frost.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger has passed in warm soil, or start indoors a few weeks early for earlier bloom.

directions: Chippendale bears 2-inch single blooms in a striking mahogany-red with golden-yellow petal tips, giving each flower a sunset-like bicolor effect on compact, bushy plants. It shares the excellent heat tolerance and drought tolerance of other Zinnia haageana selections, thriving in the same hot, humid conditions that stress Zinnia elegans, and shows good resistance to powdery mildew. The small, prolific flowers are a favorite of butterflies and hold up well as cut flowers picked in bunches for informal bouquets. Deadhead regularly to prolong bloom from early summer to frost.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Peter Pan Zinnia (Compact AAS-Winning Dwarf Double-Flowered Series)

planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger has passed in warm soil; this dwarf series was bred to produce large blooms on unusually compact plants.

directions: The Peter Pan series is a dwarf F1 hybrid zinnia strain bred to carry fully double, slightly ruffled blooms up to 4-5 inches wide on plants only 10-15 inches tall, an unusually large flower-to-plant ratio that earned several individual colors in the series All-America Selections awards through the 1970s. Its compact habit suits front-of-border plantings, containers, and small cutting-garden beds where taller giant zinnias would flop or crowd neighbors. Plants tolerate heat and dry spells well once established and benefit from good air circulation to limit powdery mildew in humid climates. Deadhead spent blooms regularly to keep the compact plants flowering heavily through the season.

common_name: Peter Pan Cream Zinnia (1978 AAS Winner)

planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger has passed in warm soil, or start indoors a few weeks early for earlier bloom.

directions: Peter Pan Cream is a 1978 All-America Selections winner prized for its soft ivory-cream, fully double blooms held on compact 10-15 inch plants. The pale color combines easily with brighter zinnia shades in mixed beds and small cutting-garden rows without overwhelming them. Like the rest of the Peter Pan series, it tolerates summer heat well and produces flowers disproportionately large for its dwarf habit. Regular deadheading keeps plants tidy and encourages continued bloom from early summer through frost.
